title: Becoming the first American-born Chinese composer of a symphony
summary: Jang says he composed 'The Chinese-American Symphony' honoring Chinese railroad workers; the idea germinated in his Palo Alto childhood.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’m happy to do interview part II with Jon Jang here at Hamilton College, and it’s been ten years since you were here before. What have you been doing all that time?

Well the first thing I want to mention is that I became the first Chinese-American, the first American born Chinese to compose a symphony which was called “The Chinese- American Symphony” that honored the Chinese railroad workers who built the first transcontinental railroad in the United States. So I’m very proud of that achievement, but I also want to recognize that that’s an important part of my legacy, my personal legacy, but as well as in America, or I would say, an advancement of American transformation.

How does something like that come about? You have this, your own passion for history, American history and the role of Chinese people in it, and you want to compose music that addresses it, but what’s the process of getting a symphony written and than having people play it?

Oh it’s been a lifelong process. And that’s actually somewhat of a separate question, but then what I would describe that this has been an idea that germinated since my childhood. During the 1960’s I spent my childhood in Palo Alto, and that’s located, that’s where Stanford University is located. And I was often reminded that Stanford built the railroad. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -1-
